people.name: Jereann Bowman
variants: Mrs. Leland Bowman (Hart and Sierra Vista yearbooks 1965-66)

life.sources: Dolan obituary 1995; Bowman High 1996 yearbook p. 6

archive.related: photograph #4801 (LW3007 reorganization plan; its index links 'Jereann Bowman 1963/69'); asset #1679 /gif/mugs/jereannbowmant.jpg (legacy mug thumbnail); article #12404 (Worden 1997, 'the old Bowman campus'). No record for Bowman High School.
archive.other: Her father Judge C.M. MacDougall has a legacy obituary page (jb_VNvalleynews082776).

valley: Came to Saugus in 1927 (Dolan 1995); came to Newhall in 1927 (Bowman 1996 yearbook); 'moving to Newhall in 1920' (Bowman 1981 yearbook). Disagreement kept.
Daughter of Judge C.M. MacDougall (Dolan 1995; Valley News 1976).
Drafted the bylaws of the Santa Clarita Valley Women's Auxiliary, the hospital volunteers, with Martha Barton and Gwen Gillespie, November 27, 1962 (Worden 2012, retrospective).
President of the Soledad Township Coordinating Council, January 1969 (Record-Press, January 8, 1969, OCR).
Driving force behind the district's continuation school, opened September 29, 1969 and named for her: Jereann Bowman High School (Dolan 1995; Bowman 1981 and 1996 yearbooks; LA Times 1989).
1973 SCV Woman of the Year, Newhall-Saugus-Valencia Chamber of Commerce (SG7301 caption; Dolan 1995; mwoty list); secretary-manager of the Chamber (Dolan 1995).
Director of the Achievement Center, 1980 (The Signal, October 8, 1980, OCR).

Lead only: ran MacDougall's Cafe at Solemint Junction ('driven by Jeriann MacDougall (Bowman)', Patricia Westcott Kelly's notes, 1990s). One recollection; not stated in a profile without another source.

sources_say: Roster: '1963' board prints four members without her; '1964-1967' board lists 'Jereann Bowman'; '1968' board does not list her; '1969' board lists 'Jereann Bowman (resigned)'.
Dolan 1995 and the Bowman 1996 yearbook: 'served on the Hart board of trustees from 1963 to 1969'.
Sierra Vista 1965 yearbook p. 4: 'Board Clerk Mrs. Leland Bowman' (the roster prints no offices before 1973).
Hart 1966 yearbook p. 15: 'Mrs. Leland Bowman' among board members.
Hart 1968 and Sierra Vista 1968 yearbooks list the board as Hoffner (clerk, the superintendent), Huntsinger, Agajanian, Ross, Schmidt, Duarte, without her. Agrees with the roster's 1968 board.

Canyon High dedication program, October 15, 1969 (as reprinted 2018): board Huntsinger, Agajanian, Bowman, Duarte, Schmidt. So she was on the board, or still printed as on it, in October 1969; the resignation came later in the 1969 board year.
board.disagreement: Start: 1963 (obituary, 1996 yearbook) against the roster's first listing in 1964-1967 (its 1963 board has a vacant fifth seat, which fits a 1963 appointment). Continuity: the obituary's '1963 to 1969' against the roster and both 1968 yearbooks, which leave her off in 1968. Footnote both; state neither. Resignation date not found.

life.sources: Not found. No obituary on the mirror or in the LA Times archive searched.

archive.related: photographs #4609 (LW2866, Agajanian hog farm 1953, with Worden's 2017 text), #5245 (J.C. Agajanian profile), #4153 (1969 chamber roster: 'Maxine Agajanian', director). No holding for Castaic Lake Water Agency or Newhall County Water District.

valley: Managed the family hog ranch near Saugus (Haskell Canyon) for his father James T. Agajanian: 'Eli, manager of the hog ranch near Saugus' (Champion Spark Plug advertisement, 1953, transcribed on LW2866).
Founded Blue Barrel Disposal Co. to haul food waste to the hog farm, and sold it in the 1960s (Worden 2017, citing Nazareth Chobanian, personal communication, 2017: retrospective).
Founder and board chairman of Santa Clarita National Bank, opened in the mid-1960s; retired as chairman in 1975 (LA Times 1987; Canyon Call 1972; COC yearbook 1973; Dan Hon 1995).
Director of the Upper Santa Clara Valley Water Agency, later Castaic Lake Water Agency, 1967-1974 (SCVHistory.com CLWA directors list; Worden 2017).
Member of the committee that became the Henry Mayo Newhall Memorial Hospital board, 1970 (Worden 2012); honored as a hospital founder, 1985 (LA Times).
General co-chairman of the Citizens' Committee to Complete College of the Canyons for the bond election of February 6, 1973 (The Canyon Call, October 31, 1972; COC 1973 yearbook).
COC Foundation Silver Spur award, 1990 (SCVHistory.com list; Worden 2017).
Newhall County Water District director: incumbent re-elected November 2, 1993, third of six for three seats with 1,592 votes (LA Times, November 4, 1993).
Had served in the Army by the years after World War II, in an anecdote about a bank loan (Dan Hon 1995).

people.name: Thomas Hanson
valley: 'A Newhall engineer' when elected (The Signal, September 16, 1970).

people.name: Louis Brathwaite

life.sources: Sevanian and Wormser obituary, The Signal, November 15, 2001 ('died Tuesday'); SCVHistory.com timeline (1933 April 25; 2001 November 13).

archive.related: candidacies #21996 (City Council, November 3, 1987) and #22092 (April 9, 1996); documents #28303 (Planning Commission 1988-1990 excerpt) and #28310 (Suomisto, The Signal, January 4, 1987). No Planning Commission office holding.

valley: Moved to the valley in 1969; Valencia resident (obituary; Signal 1987).

Federal property administrator (LA Times 1987-88); management posts with the U.S. Air Force, 38 years, retired 1990; U.S. Naval Air Reserve; designed office furniture and sold computers (obituary; 'owner of a computer furniture firm', Signal 1987).
Saugus High parent advisory committee, then elected to the Hart board (obituary, Boyer's account).
Master of ceremonies of College of the Canyons' Black History program as 'clerk of the Board of Trustees of the William S. Hart School District' (The Canyon Call, 1977-78).

City Formation Committee steering committee member; resigned it in August 1987 to run for the first City Council; lost (November 3, 1987) (LA Times June, August, September, October 1987; Signal 1987).
Inaugural Santa Clarita Planning Commissioner, appointed by Carl Boyer, January 1988; served until 1998, longer than any other commissioner (LA Times, January 30, 1988; obituary; Boyer 2015).
Ran again for City Council April 9, 1996: sixth of thirteen, 986 votes (LA Times, April 11, 1996).

Boys & Girls Club board (facilities chair); SCV Committee on Aging board, credited with the Bouquet Canyon Seniors housing; president of the Monteverde Homeowners Association (obituary). Boys & Girls Club board member 1993 (tribute program).
Wrote an autobiography, 'Black Man's Job, White Man's World', completed a week before his death (obituary). Not found published.

Boyer, in the obituary: Ruth Newhall offered to present him as 'the first black candidate for political office in the Santa Clarita Valley', and he declined the label. A 'first' claim at second hand: attribute to Boyer, and do not state it as fact without another source.
